title: Simulation with Unused Memory
statement: Let $A$ be a memory-augmented register program, let $l_0$ be its initial state, let $D$ be a decider machine, let $q_0$ assign an initial decider state to each decider, and fix a Boolean value $\beta$. Let $c$ be a configuration of the deterministic compiled machine, let $M:\mathbb Z\to\{0,1\}$ be a memory tape, let $p\in\mathbb Z$ be its head position, and let $T$ be a natural number. Assume that at every time $t<T$, whenever the deterministic run from $c$ is in a state $q$, the program has no memory instruction at $q$. Then, for every $t\le T$, the compiled memory-augmented machine started from the configuration obtained by adding memory tape $M$ with head at $p$ agrees with the deterministic run at time $t$, with that same memory tape and head position attached.
